name: Gallurese

ancestors.notes: Gallurese is classified genetically as southern Corsican / Corso-Sardinian transitional: 'predominantly Corsican on a phono-morphological level' (Maxia), sharing co's Italo-Romance grapheme conventions (chj/ghj palatals, gemination) rather than sc's.
Sardinian adstrate: centuries of contact with Logudorese Sardinian contributed roughly a third of Gallurese vocabulary and syntactic patterns (Maxia), even though the phono-morphology stays Corsican.

notes: Gallurese (gadduresu), ISO 639-3 sdn, spoken in Gallura, northeastern Sardinia. Corsican-derived (southern Corsican dialect group / Corso-Sardinian transitional variety), not a Sardinian dialect — 'predominantly Corsican on a phono-morphological level' but 'predominantly Sardinian on a syntactic level' with heavy Logudorese/Catalan/Spanish lexical influence (Maxia). Cited surface shifts relative to Corsican: Latin -LL- > [ɖː] spelled <dd> (casteddu 'castle', coraddu 'coral'; same retroflex-geminate outcome as Sardinian sc's <dd>), non-final <r> before a consonant frequently realised as [l] (poltu 'port'), and the Corsican palatal digraphs <chj>/<ghj> ([c]/[ɟ]) as in ghjesgia 'church', occhji 'eyes'. Plurals mark with -i (Corsican/Italian pattern) rather than Sardinian -s. Wired with graphemes_base/allophones_base co (Corsican) so the shared Italo-Romance consonant and vowel inventory is inherited, overriding only the cited Gallurese-specific outcomes; the wider grapheme inventory (unstressed-vowel reduction, full gemination table, precise <r>/<l> conditioning) is not recoverable from the sources fetched this session and is left to inherit from Corsican rather than guessed.
